keySections.title: What agreements are contracts
keySections.summary: All agreements are contracts if made by free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration and lawful object.

keySections.title: Agreement in restraint of trade, void
keySections.summary: Every agreement by which anyone is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business is to that extent void (Percept D'Mark standard).

keySections.title: Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void
keySections.summary: Restricting party absolutely from enforcing rights or limiting time within which he may enforce rights is void.

keySections.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
keySections.summary: Party who suffers from breach entitled to compensation for proximate losses; remote and indirect loss not recoverable unless specifically contemplated.

keySections.title: Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for
keySections.summary: Court awards reasonable compensation not exceeding amount named; punitive penalty clauses unenforceable (Fateh Chand standard).

keySections.title: Power to refer parties to arbitration where there is an arbitration agreement
keySections.summary: Judicial authority shall refer parties to arbitration unless prima facie no valid arbitration agreement exists.

keySections.title: Interim measures, etc. by Court
keySections.summary: Party may apply to a Court for interim preservation of goods, amounts, or interim injunctions before or during arbitral proceedings.

keySections.title: Appointment of arbitrators
keySections.summary: High Court / Supreme Court appointment of arbitrators upon failure of agreed procedure.

keySections.title: Grounds for challenge - Ineligibility under Seventh Schedule
keySections.summary: Any person whose relationship with the parties or counsel falls under Seventh Schedule ineligible to be appointed as arbitrator (Perkins Eastman test).

keySections.title: Application for setting aside arbitral award
keySections.summary: Recourse to Court against arbitral award on grounds of patent illegality, public policy, or lack of jurisdiction.

keySections.title: Appealable orders
keySections.summary: Appeals against orders granting or refusing interim measures or setting aside awards.

centralStatutes.status: In Force w.e.f. 1 July 2024 (Replaces Indian Evidence Act 1872)

keySections.title: Admissions in civil cases when relevant
keySections.summary: No admission is relevant in civil cases if made upon express condition that evidence of it is not to be given (without prejudice).

keySections.title: Admissibility of electronic or digital records
keySections.summary: Electronic or digital records have the same legal effect and validity as paper documents.

keySections.title: Admissibility of electronic records and certificate requirements
keySections.summary: Mandatory certificate signed by system custodian/manager with SHA-256/audit trail required for electronic records produced without primary device.

centralStatutes.status: In Force w.e.f. 1 July 2024 (Replaces Indian Penal Code 1860)

keySections.title: Criminal conspiracy
keySections.summary: Agreement of two or more persons to commit illegal act.

keySections.title: Criminal breach of trust
keySections.summary: Dishonest misappropriation or conversion of entrusted property (formerly IPC 405/406).

keySections.title: Cheating
keySections.summary: Deceiving person dishonestly to deliver property (formerly IPC 415/420).

centralStatutes.status: In Force w.e.f. 1 July 2024 (Replaces Code of Criminal Procedure 1973)

keySections.title: When police may arrest without warrant
keySections.summary: Procedural safeguards and notice of appearance (formerly CrPC 41/41A, Arnesh Kumar rule).

keySections.title: Information in cognizable cases (Zero FIR)
keySections.summary: Mandatory registration of FIR for cognizable offences regardless of jurisdiction (formerly CrPC 154).

keySections.title: Bail in non-bailable offences
keySections.summary: Regular bail powers (formerly CrPC 437/439).

keySections.title: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest
keySections.summary: Anticipatory bail petition before High Court or Sessions Court (formerly CrPC 438).

keySections.title: Saving of inherent powers of High Court
keySections.summary: Inherent jurisdiction of High Court to quash abusive proceedings (formerly CrPC 482).

keySections.title: Definition of Commercial Dispute
keySections.summary: Exhaustive categories of commercial disputes including mercantile documents, intellectual property, and service agreements.

keySections.title: Pre-Institution Mediation and Settlement
keySections.summary: Mandatory pre-institution mediation unless suit contemplates urgent interim relief (Patil Automation standard).

keySections.title: Infrastructure and training
keySections.summary: Dedicated procedures, strict written statement deadlines (120 days forfeiture rule).

keySections.title: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc., of funds
keySections.summary: Statutory notice within 30 days and 15-day cure period before criminal liability arises.

keySections.title: Offences by companies
keySections.summary: Vicarious liability of directors in charge of and responsible for the conduct of company business.

keySections.title: Power to direct interim compensation
keySections.summary: Court may order drawer to pay interim compensation not exceeding 20% of cheque amount.

keySections.title: Courts to try all civil suits unless barred
keySections.summary: Civil courts have plenary jurisdiction over suits of civil nature unless expressly or impliedly barred.

keySections.title: Other suits to be instituted where defendants reside or cause of action arises
keySections.summary: Territorial jurisdiction determined by residence, place of business, or where cause of action wholly or partially arises.

keySections.title: Temporary injunctions and interlocutory orders
keySections.summary: Triple test: Prima facie case, balance of convenience, and irreparable injury.

centralStatutes.status: Historical Code (Applicable to proceedings instituted prior to 1 July 2024)

keySections.title: When police may arrest without warrant
keySections.summary: Statutory safeguards and subjective satisfaction requirement (Arnesh Kumar standard).

keySections.title: Information in cognizable cases
keySections.summary: Mandatory registration of First Information Report (Lalita Kumari benchmark).

keySections.title: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest
keySections.summary: Anticipatory bail jurisdiction before High Court and Court of Session.

keySections.title: Saving of inherent powers of High Court
keySections.summary: Inherent jurisdiction of High Court to prevent abuse of process of any court.

centralStatutes.status: Historical Code (Applicable to offences committed prior to 1 July 2024)

keySections.title: Punishment of criminal conspiracy
keySections.summary: Conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment.

keySections.title: Punishment for criminal breach of trust
keySections.summary: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both.

keySections.title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
keySections.summary: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.

centralStatutes.status: Historical Enactment (Applicable to trials prior to 1 July 2024)

keySections.title: Admissibility of electronic records
keySections.summary: Mandatory certificate under subsection (4) required for secondary electronic evidence (Arjun Panditrao Khotkar standard).

keySections.title: Admissions in civil cases when relevant
keySections.summary: Exclusion of without prejudice communications.

landmarkPrecedents.title: Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal
landmarkPrecedents.bench: R.F. Nariman, S. Ravindra Bhat, V. Ramasubramanian JJ. (3-Judge Bench)
landmarkPrecedents.subject: Electronic Evidence / Certificate under Sec 65B IEA / Sec 63 BSA
landmarkPrecedents.ratio: Certificate under Section 65B(4) is a mandatory condition precedent to the admissibility of evidence by way of electronic record when original device cannot be brought to court.
landmarkPrecedents.relevance: Crucial for verifying admissibility of emails, WhatsApp chats, server logs and digital recordings under BSA Section 63.

landmarkPrecedents.title: Perkins Eastman Architects DPC v. HSCC (India) Ltd.
landmarkPrecedents.bench: U.U. Lalit, Vineet Saran JJ. (Division Bench)
landmarkPrecedents.subject: Arbitration / Unilateral Appointment of Sole Arbitrator
landmarkPrecedents.officialSource: Supreme Court of India Judgments Repository
landmarkPrecedents.ratio: A person who has an interest in the outcome or decision of the dispute must not have the power to unilaterally appoint a sole arbitrator under Section 12(5) read with the Seventh Schedule.
landmarkPrecedents.relevance: Standard redline detection trigger for commercial agreements and unilateral dispute resolution clauses.

landmarkPrecedents.title: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation
landmarkPrecedents.bench: Sanjay Kishan Kaul, M.M. Sundresh JJ.
landmarkPrecedents.subject: Bail Jurisprudence & Categorization of Offences
landmarkPrecedents.ratio: Strict guidelines on arrest without warrant under Sec 41/41A CrPC (now BNSS 35). Courts must strictly avoid unnecessary detention where accused cooperates and chargesheet is filed.
landmarkPrecedents.relevance: Essential benchmark for drafting Anticipatory and Regular Bail petitions.

landmarkPrecedents.title: Vidya Drolia and Others v. Durga Trading Corporation
landmarkPrecedents.bench: N.V. Ramana, Sanjiv Khanna, Krishna Murari JJ. (3-Judge Bench)
landmarkPrecedents.subject: Arbitrability & Scope of Judicial Review under Sec 8 & 11 Arbitration Act
landmarkPrecedents.ratio: Four-fold test for non-arbitrability: actions in rem, matters affecting third-party rights, inalienable sovereign functions, and disputes expressly reserved for specific courts.
landmarkPrecedents.relevance: Key defense standard in commercial suits and arbitration petitions.

landmarkPrecedents.title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
landmarkPrecedents.bench: Chandramauli Kr. Prasad, Pinaki Chandra Ghose JJ.
landmarkPrecedents.subject: Arrest guidelines under Section 41 CrPC
landmarkPrecedents.officialSource: Supreme Court of India Judgments Repository
landmarkPrecedents.ratio: Police officers cannot arrest accused merely because non-bailable offence punishable up to 7 years is alleged; objective notice of appearance must be served first.
landmarkPrecedents.relevance: Protective shield in matrimonial, financial dispute, and minor offence proceedings.

landmarkPrecedents.title: Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P.
landmarkPrecedents.bench: P. Sathasivam CJI, B.S. Chauhan, Ranjana P. Desai, Ranjan Gogoi, S.A. Bobde JJ. (5-Judge Constitution Bench)
landmarkPrecedents.subject: Mandatory Registration of FIR
landmarkPrecedents.officialSource: Supreme Court of India Judgments Repository
landmarkPrecedents.ratio: Registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 of the Code (now Section 173 BNSS) if the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence.
landmarkPrecedents.relevance: Foundational in quashing, writ petitions, and criminal defense matters.

landmarkPrecedents.title: Fateh Chand v. Balkishan Dass
landmarkPrecedents.bench: J.C. Shah, P.B. Gajendragadkar, K.N. Wanchoo, K.C. Das Gupta, J.R. Mudholkar JJ. (5-Judge Constitution Bench)
landmarkPrecedents.subject: Liquidated Damages vs Penalties under Section 74 Indian Contract Act
landmarkPrecedents.ratio: Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act dispenses with proof of actual loss, but does not justify award of compensation where no legal injury has occurred. Forfeiture of earnest money beyond reasonable loss constitutes penalty and cannot be enforced.
landmarkPrecedents.relevance: Essential benchmark for assessing liquidated damages and penalty clauses in commercial contracts.

landmarkPrecedents.title: Percept D'Mark (India) (P) Ltd. v. Zaheer Khan
landmarkPrecedents.subject: Restraint of Trade under Section 27 Indian Contract Act
landmarkPrecedents.ratio: Under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, a restrictive covenant extending beyond the term of the agreement is void and unenforceable. The doctrine of restraint of trade applies strictly post-termination.
landmarkPrecedents.relevance: Key precedent for vetting non-compete, exclusivity, and post-employment covenants.

landmarkPrecedents.title: Oil & Natural Gas Corporation Ltd. v. Saw Pipes Ltd.
landmarkPrecedents.subject: Arbitral Award Challenge & Patent Illegality under Section 34
landmarkPrecedents.ratio: An arbitral award can be set aside if it is contrary to the fundamental policy of Indian law, interest of India, or patently illegal. Liquidated damages named in contract can be granted if genuine pre-estimate.
landmarkPrecedents.relevance: Governs Section 34 arbitration award challenge petitions.
